# React rules

## Component architecture

- Give each component exactly one responsibility. A component that fetches data, transforms it, and renders UI is three responsibilities — split it.
- Separate container components (data access, state, side effects) from presentational components (pure rendering from props).
- Presentational components must be stateless and free of side effects. They receive data and emit events only.
- Never access global state, routing, or external services directly inside a presentational component.
- Compose complex UI from small, independently testable units. Prefer composition over inheritance.
- Define prop contracts explicitly. Optional props must declare a default. Avoid catch-all prop types.

## State management

- Locate state at the lowest component in the tree that needs it. Do not hoist state speculatively.
- Derive computed values from state; do not duplicate them as separate state fields.
- Server state (remote data, loading, error) and UI state (selected item, modal open) are different concerns — manage them separately.
- Mutations to server state must go through a dedicated data layer, not be applied directly to local cache.
- Side effects belong in dedicated hooks or effect layers, not inside render functions or event handlers.

## Dependency inversion and abstraction

- Access external services (APIs, storage, analytics) through an injected or imported abstraction, never via a direct SDK call inside a component.
- Data-fetching logic belongs in custom hooks or a data layer module. Components call hooks; they do not contain fetch calls.
- Routing, authentication context, and feature flags are provided via context or hooks. Components must not import router or auth SDKs directly.
- Replace concrete service bindings with injectable dependencies so components remain testable in isolation.

## Error handling and resilience

- Wrap every independently renderable section of the tree in an error boundary.
- Display a degraded but functional UI when a non-critical section fails. Do not let one section failure blank the whole page.
- Show skeleton or loading states for all async data. Never render nothing while data is loading.
- Surface user-facing errors with a recovery action (retry, reload, navigate away). Do not display raw error messages.
- Log caught errors with the correlation ID, component name, and props that contributed to the failure.

## Performance and scalability

- Code-split at route boundaries. Do not load all routes in the initial bundle.
- Memoize expensive computations and stable callback references only when profiling confirms a bottleneck. Do not memoize speculatively.
- Avoid prop drilling beyond two levels. Use context, composition, or a state layer instead.
- Keep component trees shallow. Deep nesting is a signal that responsibility boundaries are wrong.
- Images and heavy assets are lazy-loaded. Critical rendering path contains only essential resources.

## Module organisation

- Group files by feature, not by type. All modules for a feature live in one directory.
- Each feature directory exports a public API through a single index file. Consumers import from the feature, not from internal files.
- Shared utilities, hooks, and components live in a `shared/` directory and must not import from any feature.
- Circular dependencies between features are forbidden. Extract shared logic to `shared/` if two features need the same code.
